title: The k-th Largest So Far

concept.title: A min-heap of size k keeps exactly the k largest numbers
body: A **priority queue** gives the element with the **highest priority** first; a *heap* is the usual way to build one, with `push` and `pop` in O(log n) and a look at the top in O(1). Python has `heapq` (a **min**-heap on a list), C++ has `priority_queue` (a **max**-heap by default), and Java has `PriorityQueue` (a **min**-heap by default). For the opposite order, Python negates the numbers, C++ uses `greater<>` as the third template argument, and Java gives `Collections.reverseOrder()`.

To know the **k-th largest** number of a growing stream, keep only the `k` largest numbers seen so far in a **min-heap**. The smallest of these `k` numbers (the top of the heap) is exactly the k-th largest. When a new number arrives, push it; if the heap now holds `k + 1` numbers, remove the smallest one, because it can never be among the `k` largest again.
Every number costs O(log k), and the memory is O(k) instead of the whole stream. Sorting after each arrival would cost O(n log n) per step.

statement: Numbers arrive one by one. After each arrival, if at least `k` numbers have arrived, print the `k`-th largest of all numbers so far (equal numbers count separately: in 5 5 3 the 2nd largest is 5). Do not print anything while fewer than `k` numbers have arrived.
inputFormat: The second line has `n` numbers: the numbers of the stream, in the order in which they arrive.
outputFormat: `n - k + 1` lines, one for every arrival from the `k`-th on.

examples.note: After 4 5 8 the 3rd largest is 4; after 2 and after 3 it is still 4; after 10 the numbers 10 8 5 are the largest three, so it is 5.

hints: Keep a min-heap that holds at most k numbers.
After pushing a number, if the heap has more than k numbers, pop the smallest.
When the heap has exactly k numbers, its top is the k-th largest.

explanation: A min-heap holds the k largest numbers seen so far; its top is the k-th largest. A new number is pushed, and the smallest is removed when the heap grows beyond k.
solution.complexity: Time O(n log k), space O(k).

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n, k = map(int, input().split())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

import heapq
heap = []
out = []
for x in a:
    heapq.heappush(heap, x)
    if len(heap) > k:
        heapq.heappop(heap)
    if len(heap) == k:
        out.append(heap[0])
print("\n".join(map(str, out)))
